newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close at new high in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close at new high in quiet trade.

text.p: Swedish shares closed at a new high on Monday, boosted by gains in New York and on other European bourses.
The Stockholm general index closed 0.74 percent higher at 3,164.96 after very light turnover with shares worth 2.75 billion crowns changing hands.
"It was futures traders that came in and drove the bourse up," said one broker.
Bluechips gained. Telecoms group Ericsson rose three crowns to 329 while drugs company Astra edged up 3.5 to 156 crowns.
"Astra is going up a little ahead of Losec sales figures (from the U.S.) this week. There are always those who will go in and take a chance on good figures," said one broker.
Rollerbearing maker SKF fell two crowns to 212.

The company has been earmarked by analysts as the next company in the Wallenberg empire set for restructuring. SKF rose 16 percent since Electrolux unveiled its plans on June 12 to cut 12,000 jobs and close 25 plants.
"But the closer we come to the result the more the market is expecting pallid figures," one broker said. SKF is due to publish first half results before market open on Tuesday.
